/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 04 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3628 (140)
Baltic Capesize Index: 6427 (385)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2448 (-9)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1675 (7)
Baltic Handysize Index: 900 (7)
CAPESIZE
The market closed the week on a firm note, capping off what has been a distinctly bullish run over recent sessions. The BCI 182 5TC surged by a further $3,493 today, settling at $58,294, as both the Pacific and Atlantic basins continued to provide solid support. In the Pacific, sentiment remained firm despite activity easing from the frenetic pace witnessed earlier in the week. Two major miners were reported in the C5 market, bids moved into the upper $18s while offers remained closer to $19.00, with reports emerging of a Newcastlemax fixing at $18.90. Reflecting the strength in the basin, the C5 index gained $0.978 to close at $18.958. The Atlantic also maintained a positive tone, although trading activity was comparatively subdued following several busy days. Fronthaul demand from the North Atlantic continues to be well supported, while available tonnage remains tight, providing ongoing support to rates. On C3, bids improved to around $41.00 against offers at $41.50, with the index ultimately settling $0.672 higher at $41.477.
PANAMAX
The imbalance between vessel supply and cargo demand on the trans-Atlantic routes was evident today, with fixtures concluded at lower levels. An increasing tonnage count in the North Continent, combined with softer demand, pressured rates and resulted in both the P1A and P2A moving lower. Brokers have stated that owners with prompt tonnage are now having to revise their ideas downward in an effort to attract chartering interest. In the Pacific, the market continued its upward trajectory, although momentum slowed compared with previous sessions. Nevertheless, the P5TC increased by $78 day-on-day to reach $22,035. Market participants reported a moderation in North Pacific demand, while export activity from Australia and Indonesia remained robust, providing continued support to freight rates. The Great Beryl (82,747 2023) open Dongjiakou 7/8 September was reported fixed for a North Pacific round voyage at $24,500, although some market participants suggested she may ultimately load from Australia instead.
SUPRAMAX
A largely uneventful week finished with another positive Index with the 11TC average up $87 to close the week at $21,177. Apart from the north American routes, there was little change elsewhere all week, although with the summer holidays drawing to a close, this could be taken as a good sign.

Atlantic
The Losone Topic (58,071 2016) prompt Corpus Christi went on subjects for a trip Continent, the Artemis E (63,200 2013) fixed basis SW Pass with coal to East Mediterranean at around $32-33,000 with XO and the Laura (63,399 2015) open Barranquilla 8 September went on subjects basis SW Pass delivery for grains to WC Central America with Swire, but no rate emerged. The Red Orchid (61,645 2015) SW Pass 20 September was on subjects with Oldendorff for a trip Egypt with grains at $32,000 and there was also talk of an Ultramax being fixed for petcoke from the US Gulf to the Mediterranean at $35,000 with AGBT, but there were no further details.

Asia
The Bulk Friendship (58,738 2011) Nantong 7-11 September agreed a trip Hong Kong intention steels at $17,000 with an unknown account and the Josco Huizhou (61,648 2014) prompt Lanqiao fixed a trip via North China to Chittagong intention slags at $20,000, however sources said there was a split rate involved, but details remained private. The Maryam (56,798 2011) Weihai prompt did a trip West Africa intention steels/generals at $17,000, again with an unknown split, and there was a rumour of an eco Ultramax being fixed at $21,000 to West Africa with bulk under deck plus vehicles on deck, but further details were elusive. A newbuilding Ultramax in North China apparently fixed a trip US Gulf at an initial $15,000 but the split rate was not known, and a 56,000-dwt open Brunei fixed a trip via Indonesia to the Philippines $16,000, but there were no further details.
HANDYSIZE
The market closed the week on a firm note, with levels holding up across most loading regions. The Continent and Mediterranean remained relatively steady, supported mainly by scrap business. The US Gulf and South Atlantic saw pockets of activity and stronger enquiry, with levels generally reported well above last-done fixtures. The Pacific market also held steady, with some sources pointing to tight prompt tonnage and healthy steel demand from China. On the period side, the Lucilia C (35,009 2011) was rumoured fixed for 5 to 7 months delivery passing Canakkale and redelivery Atlantic at $13,000. These conditions were reflected in the index, with the 7TC average increasing by $117 to close at $16,199.

Atlantic
The Mercurius (37,705 2010) open Baltimore was reported fixed by Cargill for a trip to the Continent at just over $16,000, while the New Nation (42,683 2025) fixed from Houston to Caldera with petcoke by Norden, although further details were not disclosed.

Pacific
The TSL Rosemary (33,191 2012) open Singapore was fixed by Oldendorff Carriers for an Australia to Southeast Asia trip with grains in the $14,000s. Meanwhile, a 37,000-dwt vessel opening nearby Singapore was placed on subjects for multiple legs in the mid/high $16,000s, although further details were not disclosed. In addition, another Handysize open North China on 12 September was placed on subjects for a trip to East Africa in the low $20,000s, again with further details lacking.

Market Fundamentals
Saraji Mine Life Extension

BHP Mitsubishi Alliance (BMA) received National Environmental Protection Agency (NEPA) approval on 2 September to extend the lifespan of its Queensland based open-cut Saraji metallurgical coal mine, until 2055, McCloskey report. This follows government approval in June for BMA’s new Saraji East underground mine, expected to produce 8 Mtpa of saleable coking and pulverised injection coal, newswires report. The newly announced extension would involve the extraction of 55 Mt of coal. In FY2026 (Jul-Jun), Saraji produced 4.0 Mt of BHP’s combined 18.6 Mt metallurgical coal, despite adverse weather earlier this year, according to the company’s latest earnings release.

stem out of Dampier on a trader's vessel for $15.30, while an operator who was last seen offered $15.80 fixed shortly afterwards for an undisclosed rate.
